claims.statement: 186 orders (about 9% of overnight allocations) are currently held in 'allocated, awaiting pickup'. This is a count of totals only (no per-order manifest); no stock is lost and no order is cancelled, only delayed.
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified authoritative count (m8_r_impact, owner observability) matches the earlier tier-1 exception-audit count (186, m8_r_exceptions) and the monitor alert's 9% figure (m8_e02); not a proxy support-contact count.
claims.limitation: Totals only; does not enumerate individual affected orders/customers, so downstream customer-facing impact (e.g. SLA breach count) is not itself quantified here.

next_action.rationale: Root-cause claim C4 (status=inferred, discriminating evidence m8_r_handoffs, no open contradiction) shows the east-node carrier feed's confirmation lag (median 47 min) exceeds the booked pickup slot's close window (30 min) for the v18 split-reservation cohort EXC-0921, so slots lapse before confirmation lands. apply_slot_correction's scope is 'reversible; scoped to the affected carrier feed's pickup slots only; run only after the lag on that feed is confirmed' - that lag is now confirmed for exactly this feed/cohort. This is more surgical than revert_allocation_ruleset (which would remove the intended east-node-priority business logic entirely, not just fix the timing defect) and is a precondition for replay_held_allocations (which requires slots to be corrected first). One cohort order that was re-booked after carrier data refreshed already received a valid slot, supporting that correcting the slot timing resolves the block.
next_action.expected_information_gain: N/A (mitigation): directly remediates the confirmed timing defect for the affected feed/cohort within the human-gate's approved scope, without touching order/queue data.
